name: v2ecoli-vecoli-comparison
title: v2ecoli ↔ vEcoli comparison
how_to_read: Grade v2ecoli against vEcoli on the multi-seed STATISTICAL card (a Welch t-test over seeds) together with the ParCa t=0 card -- those are the gold standard. The single-seed card is illustrative only: single-cell runs are stochastic, so one matched or mismatched trajectory is not evidence either way.

glossary.definition: The established Covert-lab process-bigraph whole-cell E. coli model used here as the live reference standard.
The whole-cell E. coli model developed in this workspace, graded against vEcoli for parity.
A check that both engines start from identical ParCa-derived initial states, so any later divergence is dynamics, not initialization.
The gold-standard grade -- a Welch t-test comparing the two engines' observables across multiple seeds, so parity is judged statistically rather than on one trajectory.
A two-sample test for equal means without assuming equal variances, used to decide whether v2ecoli and vEcoli distributions agree.
An alternative metabolism process both engines can swap in; one study checks parity when both use it instead of the default FBA metabolism.
A defined growth medium (e.g. basal / minimal) under which the two engines are compared; parity must hold across conditions.

biological_story:
v2ecoli and vEcoli are two implementations of the same idea: a mechanistic whole-cell model of E. coli that simulates metabolism, gene expression, replication, and division for a single cell over its cycle. vEcoli is the established Covert-lab process-bigraph model; v2ecoli is the reimplementation this workspace develops.

Because both descend from the same underlying biology and parameter pipeline (ParCa / sim_data), a faithful v2ecoli should reproduce vEcoli's growth and mass trajectories when both start from matched initial states and run the same medium -- differences then point to implementation divergences, not biology. This investigation grades v2ecoli against a live vEcoli reference on cell, dry, protein and RNA mass and growth rate across nutrient conditions, treating vEcoli as the standard the newer engine must match.
question: Does v2ecoli reproduce vEcoli across nutrient conditions?

executive.what_is_this:
Does v2ecoli reproduce vEcoli across nutrient conditions when both engines swap FBA Metabolism for MetabolismRedux? Five studies (basal, with_aa, succinate, no_oxygen, acetate) run both engines from matched ParCa initial states, single generation, 6 seeds requested per condition (5 effective vEcoli seeds; 4 for acetate), and grade v2ecoli against a live vEcoli reference on cell, dry, protein and RNA mass, and growth rate.

HEADLINE: v2ecoli reproduces genuine vEcoli under the MetabolismRedux swap across all five nutrient conditions. PARCA (t=0 initial-state match): within_tol on ALL five conditions -- both engines start from identical states. STATISTICAL (Welch t-test, gen-1): all four masses (cell, dry, protein, rna) are within_tol on ALL five conditions; no condition is graded a mismatch. Per-condition overall statistical verdict is within_tol on every axis for with_aa; basal, succinate, no_oxygen and acetate are graded drift, driven solely by the instantaneous growth-rate axis (active_RNAP/active_ribosome are ungraded -- not in the local reader's observable set).

RESULT (matched gen-1 median |delta|, standard card):
  basal      cell 0.14%  dry 0.15%  protein 0.09%  rna 0.60%  growth 10.4%
  with_aa    cell 0.86%  dry 0.86%  protein 0.13%  rna 0.34%  growth 4.3%
  succinate  cell 1.49%  dry 1.50%  protein 0.92%  rna 3.50%  growth 13.4%
  no_oxygen  cell 0.70%  dry 0.70%  protein 0.20%  rna 1.23%  growth 15.3%
  acetate    cell 0.53%  dry 0.53%  protein 1.09%  rna 2.19%  growth 12.1%

INTERPRETATION: masses are within tolerance everywhere and initial states are identical (parca within_tol on all five conditions); the only residual is a growth-rate DRIFT (amber, not a mismatch) on 4 of 5 conditions, plausibly the noisy per-tick instantaneous-growth-rate derivative at single-generation shape with ~5 seeds. Multi-generation was deferred: a pbg division bug surfaces with injected processes, so this run is single-generation by design, not by failure.

studies.name: acetate
studies.title: v2ecoli reproduces vEcoli on acetate
studies.question: Does v2ecoli reproduce vEcoli on the acetate condition?

findings.statement: RESOLVED. Acetate was the one SIGNIFICANT divergence (growth +40.2%, p=0.049). After the fix v2ecoli reproduces vEcoli on acetate NATIVELY: the significant growth mismatch is gone (now +15.9%, p=0.28, not significant) and cell/dry/RNA/protein are all within tolerance; a small non-significant growth drift remains at the seed-noise level. Root cause: the ParCa ppGpp-expression NNLS set exp_free[rpoBC operon]=0 (a non-negativity boundary solution), inverting the RNAP-core (rpoB/rpoC) nutrient response and compressing assembled APORNAP-CPLX -> active_RNAP -> rRNA/growth. The fix restores a fold-change-consistent, basal-preserving rpoBC split.

evidence.observed: before -> after fix (4-seed gen-1, Welch t): growth +40.2% (p=0.049, MISMATCH) -> +15.9% (p=0.28, drift, NOT significant); RNA +13.8% drift -> +3.6% within_tol; cell +8.1% -> +2.3% within_tol; dry +8.1% -> +2.3% within_tol; protein +2.3% -> +1.3% within_tol. Overall mismatch -> drift. Native run on the fixed ParCa cache.

studies.name: metabolism_redux_basal
studies.title: v2ecoli reproduces vEcoli with MetabolismRedux (basal)
studies.question: Does v2ecoli reproduce vEcoli on basal when both engines swap FBA Metabolism for MetabolismRedux?

findings.statement: RESOLVED (short-horizon precursor run, 1 seed x 1 gen x 300 steps). The v2-side tick-2 hang was a GlobalClock zero-advance deadlock, NOT a step-cascade non-convergence (the earlier theory was a downstream symptom). MetabolismRedux is a vivarium Step but was injected as an interval pbg process, so its next_update_time output applied a tick late and GlobalClock.calculate_timestep pinned at 0. Fixed in v2ecoli PR #389 (inject vivarium Step subclasses as pbg steps). v2ecoli now runs 301 redux steps in ~125 s and REPRODUCES genuine vEcoli on basal within_tol on all graded axes (worst matched-time median |delta| = 0.79%). This study now runs the full 2-seed x 3-gen x 15000-step shape; the perf-blocker finding is carried forward as historical context for the injection fix, not yet re-validated at this shape.

evidence.observed: ROOT CAUSE (pinned by direct measurement, 2026-07-26): GlobalClock.calculate_timestep returns min(next_update_time - global_time) over the next_update_time map; it advances sim time by that full_step. MetabolismRedux (vivarium Step, update_condition-gated) inherits FBA metabolism's topology so its next_update_time wires to ('next_update_time','metabolism'). The inject bridge set as_step only from an explicit _force_step attr (which redux lacks), so redux was injected as an interval pbg PROCESS. As a process its next_update_time output is deferred to front-time global_time+interval and applies one tick late; at tick 2 nut['metabolism']==global_time==1.0 => calculate_timestep returns 0 => global_time frozen => _run_inner spins (~170k apply_updates rounds/tick). A probe recorded 4001/4001 zero-advance clock calls, argmin always the orphaned 'metabolism' key. FBA metabolism does not hang because it is built as partitioned Requester/Evolver STEPS (applied immediately in the cascade). FIX: _should_inject_as_step(cls) returns True for vivarium Step subclasses (PartitionedProcess already rejected as 'partitioned', so plain Processes stay processes); as a step the deriver applies within the tick so next_update_time advances before the clock recomputes. VERIFIED: redux basal advances global_time normally at ~0.4 s/tick; matched-timepoint gen-1 grade vs genuine vEcoli -- cell_mass 0.10%, dry_mass 0.10%, protein_mass 0.07%, rna_mass 0.52%, growth_rate 0.79% => within_tol all axes. See memory project_metabolism_redux_tick2_hang. (Supersedes the earlier STEP-CASCADE NON-CONVERGENCE theory and the missing project_metabolism_redux_injection_ode_stiffness memory.)

studies.name: no_oxygen
studies.title: v2ecoli reproduces vEcoli on no_oxygen
studies.question: Does v2ecoli reproduce vEcoli on the no_oxygen condition?

findings.statement: RESOLVED. no_oxygen was a borderline drift (growth +14.4%, p=0.08). After the fix v2ecoli reproduces vEcoli natively: growth drift more than halved to +6.7% (p=0.50, not significant), RNA now within tolerance (4/5 within_tol). Residual growth just outside +/-5% but non-significant. CAVEAT: 2 of 4 seeds hit a pre-existing anaerobic-FBA numerical edge (BIOTIN homeostatic target ~ -2e-6, unrelated to the rpoBC fix); graded on the clean seeds. Root cause: the ParCa ppGpp-expression NNLS set exp_free[rpoBC operon]=0 (a non-negativity boundary solution), inverting the RNAP-core (rpoB/rpoC) nutrient response and compressing assembled APORNAP-CPLX -> active_RNAP -> rRNA/growth. The fix restores a fold-change-consistent, basal-preserving rpoBC split.

Overall drift -> drift (4/5 within_tol, non-significant).
